extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, judges, and law students (those litigating or studying reissued patents)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and legal criteria governing when and how a United States patent may be surrendered and re-issued, the scope of the Commissioner of Patents' authority, limits on amendments, and what courts may review or collaterally attack in suits for infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner empowered to grant reissue when defects arose without fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents, who has entire control over the language of a patent, acts within his jurisdiction in granting a re-issue provided that the defects in the original patent arose without fraud, through inadvertence, accident, or mistake, and that no new matter is embraced in the re-issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner must judge sufficiency of the original specification and whether defects resulted from unintentional error; his decision is presumed correct and historically has been treated as final except in certain circumstances (e.g., fraud or clear excess of jurisdiction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory grounds for reissue (inoperative/invalid from defect or over-claiming)
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue can only be had when the original patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of (1) a defective or insufficient specification, or (2) the patentee claiming as his own more than he had a right to claim as new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The error which is sought to be corrected must have arisen by inadvertence, accident, or mistake, and without any fraudulent or deceptive intention. The re-issue statute was intended to protect against accidents and mistakes and is to be so restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issued patent must not embrace any new matter that was not in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioner includes new matter in a re-issue, that action is beyond his jurisdiction and the re-issue may be declared void; courts will confine a re-issue, if reasonably possible, to the subject-matter indicated in the original specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue cannot claim a different invention
rubrics_metrics.description: When the original and re-issued letters-patent disclose different inventions, the re-issue is void as an act unauthorized by the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerous cases (e.g., Giant Powder Co. v. California Vigorit Powder Co.) hold a re-issue claiming a different invention to be void; the invention in the re-issue must be the same as that in the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim amendments permitted only to express the same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Claim is part of the specification, and if defective may be amended; the Claim may be varied provided the same invention is described in both the original and re-issued patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will allow variation of claims to express the real invention but will not permit the claimant to expand the patent to cover a different invention; construction of re-issued claims is often limited to original subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of abandonment for matter not in original specification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee does not embrace by his specifications and Claim all that he might have done, the presumption of law is that he has abandoned to the use of the public everything outside of them, or at least has postponed any additional claim for further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption disfavors using reissue to recapture subject-matter intentionally omitted from the original filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee discovering new subject must seek separate patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patentee invented or discovered something beyond his original specifications and Claim, his course is not to attempt to cover it by a re-issue but to seek a separate patent for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue was intended to correct accidents and mistakes, not to extend protection to subsequently discovered new inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner’s decision final as to necessity for reissue absent fraud or jurisdictional excess
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the Commissioner that a re-issue is necessary is prima facie and in many respects final and conclusive, unless impeached for fraud, corruption, irregularity apparent on the face of the papers, or a plain repugnance between the old and new specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Commissioner’s finding is prima facie evidence of inadvertence, accident, or mistake, it may be overcome; courts often treat the Commissioner's action as final on the question of the necessity for re-issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts may review identity of invention and origin of error
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts have power to examine whether the re-issued patent and the original disclose the same invention, and to inquire into the origin of the corrected error (inadvertence, accident, mistake, or fraud); the identity of the invention and the origin of the error should be exhaustively investigated where contested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of inquiry may include documentary evidence (original and re-issued patents and Patent Office records) and, in some circumstances, extrinsic/parol evidence to establish identity or the provenance of the defect; the burden rests on those who controvert the Commissioner's finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issued patent subject to same invalidity grounds as original
rubrics_metrics.description: The courts have the power to declare the re-issued patent invalid for any of the general reasons which apply to original patents, or for the special reason that the re-issue contains matter which the Commissioner had no jurisdiction to allow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, courts will construe the re-issue to avoid invalidity and confine it to subject-matter of the original; but if claims contain unauthorized new matter they may be held invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on supplying defective specification by reissue (drawings/model exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts do not permit a defective specification to be supplied by re-issue excepting from the drawings or model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While claims may be amended, courts resist allowing re-issue to be used to supply substantive specification defects beyond what the drawings or models justify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue repeating original claims preserves their presumption of inadvertence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the re-issued patent repeats, as it normally does, one or more of the original Claims, these may be held valid, though all additional claims are rejected as beyond the scope of the amending power; the original Claims are conclusively presumed to have been made as they were through inadvertence, accident, or mistake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because re-issues commonly repeat some original claims, courts often accept those repeated claims as lawfully reissued while scrutinizing any additional or broader claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral attack for fraud in procuring reissue is generally barred
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither a re-issued nor an original patent can be collaterally attacked in an infringement suit on the ground that it was granted through the fraud either of the applicant or the Commissioner; this question can be raised only in a proceeding to repeal the patent by the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historic cases establish that fraud in obtaining a re-issue (even if shown by extrinsic evidence) does not ordinarily defeat a re-issued patent in a collateral infringement action; courts have made narrow exceptions where gross bad faith, corruption, or irregularity appears on the face of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud or corruption exceptions to finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the Commissioner’s decision is generally final, it may be impeached for fraud in his or the patentee's acts, for corruption on the part of the Commissioner, or for some irregularity apparent on the face of the papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such fraud, corruption, or facial irregularity is proved, the courts will not treat the Commissioner's acceptance of surrender and grant of re-issue as conclusive; otherwise the decision stands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay/abandonment inquiry in considering reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: An unreasonable delay in applying for a re-issue may be examined as bearing on the existence of original inadvertence, accident, or mistake; the doctrine of abandonment by delay is another mode of stating the courts' inquiry into whether the original error justified reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All circumstances attending the delay may be subjected to examination; a patentee who delays unreasonably may be presumed to have abandoned subject-matter or to have lacked inadvertence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of judicial inquiry often confined to patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: It has generally been considered that the inquiry into the Commissioner's action should be limited to the documentary evidence afforded by the original and re-issued patents and by the records of the action of the Patent Office, though in some cases parol evidence has been admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While courts often restrict themselves to the record, they may admit extrinsic evidence when necessary to determine identity of invention or origin of the defect; the extent of permissible extrinsic inquiry has been a contested topic in the authorities.
